fields.text:
ONE RECORD PER PRODUCTION DAY, for the product covered by the site's HACCP plan. Fill in the date, the product and the lot code first. Add a row at the first sealing of the run (Set-up), after any change or adjustment to the sealer, and at the end of the run. In process rows may be added at any time. The record stays a draft until the lot has been boxed, when the At boxing rows are added.

CCP 2 PROTECTS THE PRODUCT AFTER THE BAKE. A failed seal lets in air and microbial contamination and ends the product's shelf stability. The critical limits below are the HACCP plan's.

AT SEALING, LOOK AT EVERY POUCH AS IT COMES OFF THE SEALER: the seal sound, and no air in the pouch. That check is the control; the rows record it and do not replace it. Do NOT pull test a pouch that has just been sealed - the film is still warm and a good seal can be pulled open.

AT BOXING, LOOK AT EVERY POUCH AGAIN before it goes in its box. A pouch that has lost its vacuum is rejected. Pull test one cooled pouch from the lot before boxing starts.

A pouch or a pull test that fails stops the work - Section 3 says what happens next.

WHEN BOXING IS DONE, sign Section 4 and leave the entry as a draft. It is reviewed, the verification is signed, and the reviewer submits it.

fields.text:
The HACCP plan sets the vacuum level and the seal width to the sealer's specification, and gives only typical values (27 in. Hg and 5 mm). Neither has been confirmed for this site's machine. Until it is, write the gauge reading exactly as it shows - this record captures it but cannot show it as within a limit nobody has confirmed. A reading clearly out of line with earlier runs is treated as a failed check.

The visual check and the pull test ARE judged here, against the limits above.
fields.label: Two limits are not yet confirmed

sections.title: 3. If a limit was not met

fields.text:
A POUCH WITH A SEAL DEFECT OR AIR IN IT, A POUCH THAT HAS LOST ITS VACUUM AT BOXING, OR A FAILED PULL TEST:
1. Stop sealing or boxing.
2. Set the failed pouch aside. The pouches before it were each looked at; if there is any doubt about them, put them on Hold and tag them on FRM-702 under FSQM-018. A failed pull test puts the lot on Hold until the SQF Practitioner decides what is done with it.
3. Re-pouch and reseal what can be resealed, and destroy what cannot.
4. If the sealer is at fault, inspect or adjust it, then seal a pouch and look at it. Record that as an "After a change or adjustment" row before sealing restarts.
5. Notify the SQF Practitioner, and record the cause and the action on FRM-007 under FSQM-009.

Held product is not released on FRM-701 until its disposition is recorded.
